stemMd:
A district register records the following for last year:

- 200 civil cases were filed in the district.
- 120 of them were settled before trial.
- Of those 120, exactly 45 involved a written mediation agreement.
- Every case that involved a written mediation agreement was settled before trial.

Which of the following follows necessarily from these data?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Exactly 80 of the cases involved no written mediation agreement.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every case settled before trial involved a written mediation agreement.

options.label: C
options.textMd: More than half of the cases settled before trial involved a written mediation agreement.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Exactly 45 of the 200 cases involved a written mediation agreement.

explanationMd:
The load-bearing datum is the last one: **every** case with a written mediation agreement was settled before trial. That means the cases with an agreement form a subset of the 120 settled cases — none of them can be hiding among the 80 cases that were not settled before trial.

So the total number of cases with an agreement equals the number of such cases inside the settled group, and that number is given: 45. Option B states exactly this.

The arithmetic of the four groups, once you have it, is:

- settled with an agreement: $45$
- settled without an agreement: $120 - 45 = 75$
- not settled before trial (none of which can have an agreement): $200 - 120 = 80$
- total with no agreement: $75 + 80 = 155$

**How to check.** Add the parts back up: $45 + 75 + 80 = 200$, which matches the stated total, so no case has been counted twice or dropped. Then reread the fourth datum and confirm you have used it in the direction it is written — it constrains where agreement cases can be, not where settled cases must be.

distractorRationale.c: 45 out of 120 is 37.5 per cent, which is less than half. This option comes from reading '45' as a large share of the settled group without comparing it to 120, or from comparing 45 to the 80 unsettled cases instead.
distractorRationale.a: 80 is the number of cases not settled before trial. It is true that none of those 80 had an agreement, but 75 of the settled cases had none either, so the correct figure is 155. This option stops at the first group it finds with no agreements.
distractorRationale.b: This reverses the fourth datum. 'Every case with an agreement was settled' does not license 'every settled case had an agreement'; in fact 75 of the 120 settled cases did not. Confusing a statement with its converse is the classic error here.

accessibilityText: A data propositions question. A register records 200 civil cases filed, of which 120 were settled before trial; of those 120, exactly 45 involved a written mediation agreement; and every case involving a written mediation agreement was settled before trial. The question asks which of four statements follows necessarily.

provenance.notes: Original item on the published Bocconi Law syllabus entry 'data propositions': judging which statements do and do not follow from the data supplied. All figures are invented.

review.author: bocconi-law-wave3-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Every written-agreement case was settled, and among the 120 settled exactly 45 had one, so the total number of written-agreement cases among the 200 is exactly 45. A is false (200 - 45 = 155, and 120 - 45 = 75, neither is 80), B is false, C is false since 45 of 120 is under a half.

review.notes: Author's working: agreement cases are a subset of the settled cases, so the total with an agreement is 45 (option B). A is false because 45/120 = 37.5 per cent; C is false because 155 cases had no agreement; D is the converse of the given conditional and is contradicted by the 75 settled cases without an agreement. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
